rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence to guide exploitation. The most important first step is to establish a clear, interpretable performance baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: a single RNA profile encoded with standard PCA, no aggregation, no fusion. This gives a clean reference accuracy against which all subsequent design choices (multiprofile aggregation, learned encoders like scVI/SCGPT, image modality, and multimodal fusion) can be compared. Establishing this floor first reduces uncertainty about the task difficulty and prevents misattributing gains to complex components when a simple model already performs well. With 9 experiments remaining, this baseline anchors the search and lets subsequent experiments isolate the marginal contribution of each design axis.

The RNA-only PCA baseline (config_001) achieved only 0.485 accuracy, which is very low and could reflect either an uninformative RNA representation or a fundamentally difficult task. The most critical uncertainty at this stage is whether the image modality carries stronger predictive signal than RNA. Testing config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the modality question while keeping the profile setting (singleprofile) and model complexity comparable to the RNA baseline. If image accuracy substantially exceeds 0.485, it directs remaining budget toward image-centric or multimodal configurations; if it is similarly low, it suggests the task is inherently hard and we should focus on learned encoders and aggregation strategies. This single comparison maximally reduces uncertainty about which modality to prioritize before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile designs.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, far outperforming image-only ResNet50 (config_010) at 20.8%. This establishes RNA as the dominant modality and makes it the priority for improvement. Uncertainty: We have no data on whether multiprofile (multiple spatial profiles per cell) adds discriminative signal beyond a single profile. This is a foundational design choice that gates many downstream configurations. This experiment (config_002) tests multiprofile + avgpool aggregation with the same PCA n2000 encoder, isolating the effect of multiple profiles with the simplest aggregation. It is the minimal, clean extension of our best result (one conceptual change: single→multiprofile), making the comparison directly interpretable. If multiprofile helps, it justifies investing remaining budget in multiprofile variants (transformer aggregation, learned encoders, multimodal fusion); if it doesn't, we can focus on single-profile encoder improvements. With 7 experiments left, resolving this structural question early maximizes information value for the rest of the search.

Evidence: config_002 (RNA, multi-profile, PCA, avgpool) achieved 0.591 acc, a large jump over config_001 (single-profile, 0.485), confirming multi-profile is the dominant gain. Image-only (config_010, 0.208) is very weak, so fusion gains are uncertain. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for the same multi-profile PCA representation. This experiment (config_003) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_002, isolating the aggregation choice (transformer vs avgpool) while holding encoder and profile setting fixed. This is the best use of the next slot because it directly extends our strongest result, resolves a key design decision before committing to multimodal or alternative-encoder experiments, and the outcome will inform whether to pursue transformer aggregation in later, more complex configurations.

Evidence: The current best is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile+avgpool is a strong setup and RNA dominates over image (0.208). However, all RNA experiments so far use PCA, a linear encoder. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) could further improve the RNA representation in the best-performing multiprofile+avgpool setting. This experiment (config_005) isolates the RNA encoder variable by keeping profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool identical to config_002, directly testing whether scvi_n200 outperforms pca_n2000. This is the best use of the next experiment because establishing the optimal RNA encoder is a foundational decision that informs all subsequent multimodal experiments; with 5 experiments remaining, resolving this uncertainty first ensures that any multimodal tests in later experiments use the strongest RNA backbone.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy, showing a clear progression from PCA single (0.485) → PCA multi+avgpool (0.591) → scvi multi+avgpool (0.650). RNA dominates over image (0.208). Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether scgpt, the third available RNA encoder, outperforms scvi_n200 under the same optimal settings. This experiment (config_008: scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool) isolates the encoder effect while holding profile setting and aggregation at their best-known values, providing a clean single-variable comparison to config_005. If scgpt improves, it gives a stronger RNA baseline for potential multimodal fusion in remaining experiments; if not, it confirms scvi_n200 as the best encoder and redirects remaining budget toward multimodal exploration or other refinements. This is the highest-information, lowest-risk next step with 4 experiments left.

The best result so far is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy. The key uncertainty is whether adding an image modality—particularly with a stronger encoder (ViT-L vs. the weak resnet50 that scored only 0.208)—can complement the strong RNA signal and push accuracy higher. Config_036 isolates this question by keeping the proven-best RNA setup (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) and adding imagenet_vit_l with concat fusion. If it exceeds 0.650, the remaining 3 experiments can refine the multimodal direction (e.g., weighted fusion, transformer aggregation). If it does not, we confirm RNA-only dominance and can spend remaining budget on RNA-only refinements (e.g., config_006 transformer aggregation with scvi_n200). This is the highest-information experiment for the limited budget because it resolves the central question of whether multimodality adds value given the current evidence that image alone is very weak.

The best result so far is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.715 accuracy, a substantial jump over the best RNA-only (0.650). The key remaining question within this top-performing family is whether the fusion strategy matters: concat simply stacks features, while weighted fusion allows learned per-modality weighting. Config_037 is a single-variable change (concat → weighted) from the best result, directly isolating the fusion effect. This is the highest-value test because (1) it exploits the strongest evidence (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + multiprofile), (2) it changes only one design choice so any accuracy shift can be attributed to fusion, and (3) with only 2 experiments remaining after this one, confirming or improving the fusion method is the most efficient path to either locking in the best config or discovering a further gain before the budget ends.

The current best is config_036 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) at 0.7150. In RNA-only experiments, avgpool outperformed transformer aggregation (config_002 vs config_003), but that was with pca_n2000 and a single modality. The interaction between transformer aggregation and the richer scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l multimodal representations is untested. Config_038 changes only the aggregation (avgpool→transformer) while keeping all other settings identical to the best config, providing a clean single-variable comparison. If transformer helps in the multimodal context, it could push accuracy above 0.7150; if not, it confirms avgpool is optimal and gives us high confidence in config_036 as the final answer. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, isolating the aggregation effect on the current best configuration is the highest-value use of the slot.

The best result so far is config_038 (0.7207: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat). The evidence strongly favors scvi_n200 as RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l as image encoder, multiprofile, and concat over weighted fusion (0.7150 vs 0.7062 with avgpool). Config_039 (transformer + weighted) is the only untested cell in the 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid for this top-performing family. As the final experiment, it completes the characterization of the best configuration space and tests whether the small concat-over-weighted gap seen with avgpool holds or reverses under transformer aggregation. While the expected gain is modest, it is the most targeted exploitation of the strongest evidence and the only remaining untested variant in the proven best family, making it the best use of the last budget slot.
